newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RUGBY-RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND OUT TO PROVE POINT AGAINST PUMAS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND OUT TO PROVE POINT AGAINST PUMAS.

text.p: A makeshift England will seek on Saturday to erase the memory of their unconvincing home win against Argentina late last year and also the doubts raised by a wobbly start to their tour.

Coach Jack Rowell picked six uncapped players in the 15 for the first of two tests, including Jim Mallinder, whose safe pair of hands and blazing try made him England's best player in their slipshod loss to Buenos Aires.
Alex King and Mark Mapletoft, who managed to miss eight out of 10 kicks for penalties and conversions against Buenos Aires, are out of the 15, although Mapletoft scraped in as a substitute.

England started the tour with a workmanlike yet unspectacular 38-21 win against Argentine champions Cordoba, but then fell to traditional giant-killers Buenos Aires 23-21. They recovered to squash Argentina "A" 58-17 on Tuesday.

England only just managed to avoid a humilliating loss to the Pumas at Twickenham last December, as hooker Mark Regan wriggled out from beneath a pile of bodies to score his first international try eight minutes from the end.
Argentina also pushed England during the 1995 World Cup, outscoring them on tries by two to nil despite losing 24-18.

Rowell has said he fears the Argentines' tough pack and strong scrummaging could unsettle the England side, much of whose playing blood has been drained to feed the British Lions squad in South Africa.

Yet Argentine rugby, whose traditionalist union is one of the few in the world still amateur and is now losing players to paying clubs in England and Australia, has had a long dry spell since the glory days of Hugo Porta in the 1980s.
Three of the Pumas play for English clubs. Flanker Rolando Martin signed in March for Richmond, while forwards German Llanes and Federico Mendez play for Bath.
Puma coach Jose Luis Imhoff has made only three changes to the side which played at Twickenham.
England's biggest December headache, fly-half Gonzalo Quesada, who kicked six penalties in the Twickenham match which ended 20-18, will be against them again on Saturday.
The match is due to start at 1530 local time in the Ferro Carril Oeste stadium in Buenos Aires.

England: Jim Mallinder, Jon Sleightholme, Phil de Glanville (captain), Nick Greenstock, Adedavo Adebayo, Mike Catt, Kyran Bracken, Tony Diprose, Ben Clarke, Martin Corry, Nigel Redman, Martin Haag, Darren Garforth, Phil Greening, Kevin Yates.

Argentina: Ezequiel Jurado, Tomas Solari, Eduardo Simone, Lisandro Arbizu, Facundo Soler, Gonzalo Quesada, Nicolas Fernandez Miranda, Pablo Bouza, Pablo Camerinckx, Rolando Martin, Pedro Sporleder, German Llanes, Mauricio Reggiardo, Federico Mendez, Ronerto Grau.
